overall_summary: Initial performance data shows a strong correlation between simple, high-recognition trivia (Geography/Space) and higher retention. 'Quick' and 'Easy' concepts are currently outperforming abstract logic puzzles, suggesting the audience prefers instant gratification over prolonged mental effort.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'Largest ocean' and 'Red Planet' maintain high average percentage watched compared to complex logic puzzles.
winning_patterns.action: Prioritize rapid-fire, high-recognition trivia categories to maintain velocity and viewer interest.

improvements.evidence: Retention curves show a steep drop-off within the first 5-10% of videos (the 'hook' phase).
improvements.action: Reduce intro text and get to the A/B/C/D question within 1.5 seconds of the video start.

retention_insights.evidence: Average view percentages peak near 50-75% for content like 'Largest Ocean'.
retention_insights.action: Implement a 15-second loop format to encourage re-watches and boost algorithmic signals.

best_posting_windows.reason: Aligned with early morning engagement observed in geography and science categories.
Consistent with strong performance in lunch-hour browsing patterns.

next_best_quiz_directions.reason: Space-themed content currently shows the most consistent engagement.
